terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: The source is flat icon art rather than a photographed camera view. Use a long-lens frontal camera to approximate orthographic projection and confirm framing through screenshot comparison.

objectClass.notes: Observed as a flat 400x400 mascot icon. Route as a custom object-like procedural creature because img2threejs v1.4.1's character template is humanoid-only; using it would invent a torso, neck, clothing, arms, and legs. The model remains a stylized character interpretation, not an exact hidden-side reconstruction. Character settings supply the wooden mallet and confirm the character flies with no legs.

reasoning: The source silhouette is simple, but the runtime hierarchy needs independent pivots for hover, trunk sway, and the BONK mallet swing.
Two paired feature systems (ears and eyes), a rear color cap, a curved trunk, and a compound wooden mallet make the implementation moderate rather than simple.
The single flat view hides depth, rear-cap wrap, appendage roots, and mallet placement, so inferred regions must retain explicit confidence notes.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Moderate depth is required to keep the rounded body, face systems, appendage pivots, and mallet assembly separately addressable without turning a simple mascot into an overbuilt mesh.

acceptedInferences.description: The icon does not reveal body depth; use a shallow ellipsoid whose depth is about 58% of its visible width.
The white rear region is interpreted as a continuous rear ellipsoid cap that wraps around the hidden back.
The trunk is interpreted as a tapered tube leaving the lower-left face and curving downward and slightly forward.
The character file, not the icon, supplies the mallet. Mount a short right-side arm pivot with a detachable wooden mallet.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Dominant vivid sky-blue rounded body with a near-black silhouette rim.
White rear color zone separated from the blue body by a dark curved boundary.
Small blue rounded tail nub protrudes from the lower-right rear silhouette.
Two solid near-black circular eyes with no pupils, irises, or highlights.
Two small triangular ears break the top silhouette and contain blue inner faces.
A blue tapered trunk emerges from the lower-left face, curves downward, and has a dark outline.
A thick near-black outline surrounds the body, ears, trunk, and rear boundary.

anatomy.note: The humanoid head-unit system is not semantically applicable to this mascot. Values encode one body/head unit and the visible face layout only; implementation uses a custom legless creature hierarchy.

definitionOfDone: The front three-quarter render reads immediately as Yumemin at thumbnail size: vivid blue rounded body, pupil-free dot eyes, two small ears, flexible left-side trunk, white rear cap, and no legs.
The model remains volumetric in side and rear orbit views, with the rear cap wrapping continuously and no flat-card collapse.
Named pivots expose hover, trunk sway, and mallet swing; the mallet can be detached without affecting the body.
All visible meshes are named, clickable, and covered by the runtime parts manifest.

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: The source is flat JPEG icon art with no recoverable physical lighting. Exact sampled albedo plus authored matte response is more faithful than deriving PBR maps from compression artifacts.

mustAvoid: unjustified albedo gradients that change the flat icon identity
plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.
